newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland readies bill to help ailing coal mines.
newsitem.headline: Poland readies bill to help ailing coal mines.

text.p: Poland's economy ministry is working on a bill that would delay the coal mining sector's huge debt payments to save the ailing industry from collapse, a deputy economy minister said on Tuesday.
"The bill on financial restructuring of the mining sector will postpone mines' debt payments," Jerzy Markowski told Reuters after attending a parliamentary committee meeting.
He said the bill, likely to be submitted for government scrutiny in March, also encouraged creditors to swap debts for equity in mines.
He said it was too early to give more details.
More than 50 state-owned coal mines had debt amounting to about nine billion zlotys, and many economists say some 20 or 25 of the pits should be rapidly closed.
But the government, fearing social protests in the densely-populated mining region of Silesia, wants to extend the closures over many years and create alternative jobs.
